title: A hundred utterances, one writing
literal_meaning: A hundred utterances, one written record.
explanation: The saying sets a hundred spoken utterances beside one written record. The contrast draws attention to what a record can preserve after talk has passed. It values putting something into writing without making every written statement true or supplying a legal rule.
meaning_odia: ଶହେ ମୁହଁର କଥା ପାଖରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗୋଟିଏ ଲେଖାକୁ ରଖେ। କଥା ସରିଗଲା ପରେ ଲେଖା ରହି କଥାଟି ମନେ ପକାଇପାରେ—ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ସେହି ମହତ୍ତ୍ୱ ଦିଶେ। ଏଥିରୁ ସବୁ ଲେଖା ସତ ବା ଏହା କୌଣସି ଆଇନର ନିୟମ ବୋଲି ଧରିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Many spoken words are set beside a single lasting record.
odia_summary: ଅନେକ ମୁହଁର କଥା ପାଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଲିଖିତ କଥାର ମହତ୍ତ୍ୱ ଦିଶେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଲୋଚନା ପରେ ଦଳଟି ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଥିବା କାମଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଲେଖିଲା ଓ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ପୁଣି ପଢ଼ି ଶୁଣାଇଲା। / A group writes and checks its agreed tasks together. This application is invented.
cultural_context: ଭାକା is read here as spoken words, contrasted with ଲେଖା, something put into writing. The compressed comparison leaves its force to the listener.
